cases.sentence: Несмотря на привычку Балашева к ___, роскошь и пышность двора Наполеона поразили его.
cases.explain: «придворной торжественности» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Though Balashëv was used to imperial pomp, he was amazed at the luxury and magnificence of Napoleon’s court.

cases.sentence: Граф Тюрен ввел его в большую приемную, где дожидалось много генералов, камергеров и ___, из которых многих Балашев видал при дворе русского императора.
cases.explain: «польских магнатов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The Comte de Turenne showed him into a big reception room where many generals, gentlemen-in-waiting, and Polish magnates—several of whom Balashëv had seen at the court of the Emperor of Russia—were waiting. Duroc said that Napoleon would receive the Russian general before going for his ride.

cases.sentence: Дюрок сказал, что император Наполеон примет ___ перед своею прогулкой.
cases.explain: «русского генерала» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The Comte de Turenne showed him into a big reception room where many generals, gentlemen-in-waiting, and Polish magnates—several of whom Balashëv had seen at the court of the Emperor of Russia—were waiting. Duroc said that Napoleon would receive the Russian general before going for his ride.

cases.sentence: После нескольких минут ожидания, ___ вышел в большую приемную и, учтиво поклонившись Балашеву, пригласил его итти за собой.
cases.explain: «дежурный камергер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: After some minutes, the gentleman-in-waiting who was on duty came into the great reception room and, bowing politely, asked Balashëv to follow him.

cases.sentence: Балашев вошел в маленькую приемную, из которой одна дверь вела в кабинет, в тот самый кабинет, из которого отправлял его ___.
cases.explain: «русский император» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Balashëv went into a small reception room, one door of which led into a study, the very one from which the Russian Emperor had dispatched him on his mission. He stood a minute or two, waiting. He heard hurried footsteps beyond the door, both halves of it were opened rapidly; all was silent and then from the study the sound was heard of other steps, firm and resolute—they were those of Napoleon. He had just finished dressing for his ride, and wore a blue uniform, opening in front over a white waistcoat so long that it covered his rotund stomach, white leather breeches tightly fitting the fat thighs of his short legs, and Hessian boots. His short hair had evidently just been brushed, but one lock hung down in the middle of his broad forehead. His plump white neck stood out sharply above the black collar of his uniform, and he smelled of Eau de cologne. His full face, rather young-looking, with its prominent chin, wore a gracious and majestic expression of imperial welcome.
